value.title: Daemon: intake endpoint + enrichment through existing lanes

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Daemon intake + enrichment. Research facts that shape this: a new POST endpoint is four files (http.rs route+handler, domain module, cli client, cli main); SummarizeJob/EmbedJob carry text inline and lanes are provider-keyed so conversation jobs ride with ZERO lane config; EmbedJob.source stays raw|smart (vector-space axis untouched).

value.title: POST /conversations: daemon/src/conversations.rs module + route in http.rs; schema::guard first; envelope via answer::ok/failed so user messages ride; ITERATIVE APPEND is the contract (Jordan 2026-08-27): a conversation grows across many posts -- header upsert + turn batch, idempotent on (conversation_id, turn_no), re-post of overlap returns unchanged counts, only new turns enqueue enrichment
value.note: daemon/src/conversations.rs + POST /conversations in http.rs (ed0d660). schema::guard first, answer::ok/failed envelope, with_next_action. Iterative append is enforced by the primary key: the enqueue reads the store's ACCEPTED set, not the posted batch, so a re-post of an overlap costs nothing. Proven by a_re_post_enqueues_only_the_delta.

value.title: Payload policy ENFORCED at intake (importer shapes, intake enforces): tool outputs cut to 512B head + total_bytes + truncated flag; write-family inputs to path+length; oversize bodies covered by the w-embed-oversize per-input guard
value.note: Enforced at intake, not trusted from the client, and shaped BEFORE storage so there is no window in which the oversized bytes exist. Write-family matching is case- and namespace-insensitive (Write / write / fs.write / str_replace_editor) because a policy that catches one spelling silently stores every other harness's file bodies. Cuts never split a character - truncate panics mid-codepoint and would lose the whole batch. Tests: the_payload_policy_is_enforced_at_intake_not_trusted plus six unit tests.

value.title: Enrichment enqueue on NEWLY accepted turns only: below size gate (config, sketch 256B) raw embed only; at/above gate summarize + both embeddings; same SummarizeJob/EmbedJob shapes, dedupe keys and lanes
value.note: enrich::enqueue_for_turns, same SummarizeJob/EmbedJob shapes, dedupe keys and lanes as code - zero lane config. Gate is BYTES (indexing.turn_summary_min_bytes, default 256) because a turn is one position in a sequence, so a line floor cannot tell a five-word turn from one carrying a 4KB tool result. Proven by the_size_gate_decides_which_turns_earn_a_summary.

value.title: Identity ruling (critic finding 5): SummarizeJob/EmbedJob identity is non-optional and provider selection is per-repo -- decide + document identity for anchored conversations (anchor repo identity) AND unanchored/orphaned ones (reserved identity with documented provider fallback); orphaned-anchor case tested
value.note: RULED (Jordan via o-prime 2026-08-27) and measured against wiring.rs:169-177: anchored conversations use the anchor repo's identity; unanchored use the reserved conv:unanchored. Provider resolution is a map lookup with a default fallback, so the ORPHANED case costs zero special-case code - it misses the map and takes the default. conv: is a namespace RepoIdentity structurally cannot mint (git.rs:85-105), so no collision is possible. Proven by unanchored_and_orphaned_conversations_both_resolve_to_a_provider.

value.title: Fake-provider tests: both gate paths; iterative append enqueues only the delta; identical turns across two conversations = ONE enrichment spend; remove of the anchored repo + gc leaves conversation and chain intact
value.note: 8 tests in daemon/tests/conversation_intake.rs: both gate paths, delta-only enqueue, identical turns across two conversations costing ONE enrichment, remove-of-anchor + gc leaving the chain intact, malformed guid and turn_no 0 refused with a fix. NOTE: the gc test FAILED on first run and exposed a production defect - level-0 GC was silently deleting every pending embed job - fixed in 310ac0e with its own tests and a boot recovery sweep.
